examples.chapterTitle: Reading a moving body
examples.title: Coordinate and pose inspection
examples.task: Move the root and hand targets; distinguish authored geometry from a measured body.
examples.limits: No forces, contact, anatomical accuracy or clinical inference.

examples.chapterTitle: Force changes motion
examples.title: Force, mass and displacement
examples.task: Change net force and inspect the displacement and work at one second.
examples.limits: Constant mass and constant horizontal net force; visual arrow lengths are scaled.

examples.chapterTitle: A force has an application point
examples.title: Moment arm in three dimensions
examples.task: Change the planar lever angle and inspect the moment vector.
examples.limits: Planar mechanics rendered in 3D; no joint or anatomical inference.

examples.chapterTitle: Energy reveals numerical error
examples.title: Oscillator state and energy
examples.task: Compare explicit Euler, symplectic Euler and Verlet after the same number of steps.
examples.limits: One-dimensional oscillator rendered in 3D; numerical drift is not a checked conservation theorem.

examples.chapterTitle: Measure deformation before choosing a muscle law
examples.title: Reference and deformed tetrahedron
examples.task: Change axial stretch and shear; compare determinant with triangle-measured volume.
examples.limits: Prescribed affine map, not force equilibrium or tissue response.

examples.chapterTitle: Uneven stretch and local volume
examples.title: Uneven stretch and local volume
examples.task: Change the stretch gradient and compensation; inspect the existing closed prism mesh.
examples.limits: Algebraic local-volume claims do not prove mesh integration or floating-point refinement.

examples.chapterTitle: Connect fibre architecture to force without inventing strength
examples.title: Fibres, cuts and projected force
examples.task: Change pennation and material stretch; compare reference and current cut forces.
examples.limits: Authored areas/stresses; one projection only; no contraction or calibrated muscle prediction.

examples.chapterTitle: Let material stiffness and boundaries choose the lateral shape
examples.title: Free and confined compression
examples.task: Change height stretch and inspect free versus confined lateral response.
examples.limits: Existing homogeneous one-lateral-DOF equilibrium; not unrestricted 3D material stability.

examples.chapterTitle: Load, hold, release: storage and viscous loss
examples.title: Load, hold and recovery specimen
examples.task: Scrub the existing finite SLS protocol and compare work, storage and loss.
examples.limits: One-dimensional small-strain bar extruded for viewing; transverse area is not solved.

examples.chapterTitle: One force, unequal stretches, and local volume
examples.title: Two separate blocks in series
examples.task: Change transmitted force and compare the two solved stretches and areas.
examples.limits: Two separate homogeneous incompressible blocks and ideal spacer; not a continuous tapered body.

examples.chapterTitle: Anatomy is evidence, not a silhouette
examples.title: Anatomy as source geometry
examples.task: Select a licensed atlas structure and inspect its original surface and identity.
examples.limits: Static atlas; no posed anatomical rig or subject-matched muscle parameters.

examples.chapterTitle: Inspect real anatomy and recorded evidence
examples.title: Atlas parts and evidence streams
examples.task: Select structures and inspect units, source hashes and raw topology counts.
examples.limits: Atlas surfaces and recorded signals are independent; no inferred registration or dynamics.

examples.chapterTitle: Muscle pulls through a changing path
examples.title: Synthetic actuator geometry
examples.task: Change hinge angle and activation; inspect path length and signed moment arm.
examples.limits: Authored synthetic path and force law; no tissue shape or calibrated strength.

examples.chapterTitle: Let forces move the elbow
examples.title: Force-driven hinge inspection
examples.task: Step the existing hinge under a chosen load and inspect force and torque.
examples.limits: Fixed shoulder, single hinge and authored actuator; no anatomical validation.

examples.chapterTitle: From line forces to tissue and rendered skin
examples.title: Artistic skin and pose
examples.task: Use the independent mannequin gizmos to inspect pose-dependent rendered skin.
examples.limits: Dual-quaternion artistic deformation, not tissue mechanics; contact may interpenetrate.

examples.chapterTitle: Store tendon energy and resist compression
examples.title: Reduced tendon and tissue balance
examples.task: Inspect the existing reduced series geometry at a prescribed angle and excitation.
examples.limits: Reduced static hold; no 3D anatomical tissue solve or sliding interface.

examples.chapterTitle: From a spring to a volume of tissue
examples.title: Reference/current continuum geometry
examples.task: Shear and stretch one tetrahedron; inspect its reference/current boundaries.
examples.limits: Kinematic tensor inspection alone does not establish a constitutive law or medical validity.

examples.chapterTitle: Fast solvers and what they approximate
examples.title: Reference and finite-sweep approximation
examples.task: Change compliant sweeps on the same small linear FEM problem.
examples.limits: Existing bounded reference/compliant comparison; not an implemented reduced-basis or multigrid method.

examples.chapterTitle: Solve a spatial solid, then buy speed with a measured error
examples.title: Spatial finite-element comparison
examples.task: Inspect reference and approximation on the same tetrahedral discretization.
examples.limits: Linear small-strain, authored load and fixed mesh; visual displacement magnification is declared.

examples.chapterTitle: What does a pressure space miss?
examples.title: Weighted samples and unresolved field
examples.task: Change pressure-space resolution while holding the four prescribed samples fixed.
examples.limits: Abstract sample glyphs, not body deformation or an equilibrium pressure field.

examples.chapterTitle: Skin must follow motion without losing the mechanics
examples.title: Posing and interface boundaries
examples.task: Inspect the independent rig surface at a fixed pose using its hand/head gizmos.
examples.limits: Rig weights are presentation mappings; sliding, contact and two-way tissue coupling are not supplied.

examples.chapterTitle: Lift, release and compress a spatial arm
examples.title: One-way arm and independent skin
examples.task: Change the prescribed pose and inspect the existing capstone geometry.
examples.limits: Existing one-way quasistatic educational model; shape has no reaction feedback to the hinge.

examples.chapterTitle: Coupled tissue mechanics: a checked intermediate
examples.title: Preserved coupled-fixture trajectory
examples.task: Scrub the saved trajectory and inspect nodal geometry and its recorded work residual.
examples.limits: Read-only replay of historical authored fixture evidence; no new solve or physiological qualification.

examples.chapterTitle: Build an anatomical apparatus that can fail a check
examples.title: Anatomical apparatus and failed trajectory
examples.task: Inspect reference parts alongside the preserved failed trajectory status.
examples.limits: Reference geometry is not a successful trajectory; original rejection remains visible.

examples.chapterTitle: What the experiments establish
examples.title: Model and evidence comparison
examples.task: Switch between prescribed geometry and licensed atlas evidence; inspect what each can support.
examples.limits: No unified accuracy score, anatomical calibration or equivalence between models.

examples.chapterTitle: From a lever to an arm
examples.title: Implemented research layers
examples.task: Inspect licensed source surfaces and the separate authored apparatus geometry.
examples.limits: Stages are distinct datasets; overlay does not establish subject matching or missing mechanics.

examples.chapterTitle: Sources and evidence boundaries
examples.title: Geometry provenance inspector
examples.task: Pick a surface to inspect its source identity, units, mesh counts and licence.
examples.limits: Geometry provenance does not establish a mechanical or clinical result.
